title: Mexico's speakeasy cutting contests with Duke jotting on his cuffs
summary: Mexico's basement joint near the Lafayette Theater held piano nights with James P. Johnson, Willie the Lion and Fats Waller, and Duke only listened and wrote passages on his shirt cuffs.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Tell me about Mexico in New York.
Oh, Mexico was funny. When I first went to New York, Mexico was a speakeasy joint, you know, and --
On -- right near where, oh, -- oh, God. You heard of the Lafayette Theater, huh?
Tom Whaley told me (Inaudible) about the Lafayette Theater.
Yeah, well, it was right around the corner from the Lafayette Theater but it was down in the basement.

So in those days they used to call them "cutting contests." You know, like instead of a jam session. So I had just gotten to -- I hadn't been in New York long -- so Luis Russell told me, he said, "C'mon, we're going to go into the cutting contest." I said, "What do you mean, cutting contest?" He said, "You'll see."

And this night was piano night. James P. Johnson, Willie the Lion. They had Duke in there and Fats Waller. All the biggies, you know. And Mexico had his little bar and on the back of the bar was all the hammers to hit the strings, you know, in the piano, because when the Lion would get up there,
he'd -- the Lion's going to roar and he'd bang the piano and all these hammers would fly out there and they'd pick them up and start putting them back in there.

Well, this night Duke was in there. He wouldn't play nothing. He just listened and started writing things on his sleeves. He had tuxedo cuff sleeves and he was writing, writing little passages that he liked, and he was stealing like that, you see? And then next night would be like a trombone night. It was wonderful, a lot of fun.
To your knowledge, did any of those piano players ever recognize their material?
Did they ever say anything to Duke?

No, because they -- He was nothing. He couldn't join that bunch. That bunch was supposed to be the elite of the pianists and Duke was there to just listening. He was just like -- trying to steal -- some kid or something trying to learn something, which he was.
